answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The bridge multiplier is published, charged in delta, and marble lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2980 identities would post 3666 proofs and burn roughly 25 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
